title: Constructible subsets of a spectral space are open and closed in the constructible topology
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and let $E\subseteq X$ be a constructible subset [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Then $E$ is both open and closed in the constructible topology of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] (the topology on $X$ with subbase the quasi-compact open subsets of $X$ and their complements).

source.place: Paragraph after Definition 08YG (definition-spectral-space), line 4290 ff.: 'since X is spectral an open U is retrocompact iff U is quasi-compact; hence the constructible topology can also be characterized as the coarsest topology such that every constructible subset of X is both open and closed'; with Lemma 005H (lemma-constructible, line 2571: constructible subsets form a Boolean algebra) and Lemma 0069 (lemma-topology-quasi-separated-scheme, line 5470, (2): a quasi-compact open is retrocompact)

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq X$ be open. Then $U$ is retrocompact in $X$ if and only if $U$ is quasi-compact, because $X$ is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-open-retrocompact-iff-quasi-compact]. Hence, by Definition 005G as recorded in [def-weil-constructible-subset], $E=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}(U_i\cap(X\setminus V_i))$ for some $n\ge 0$ and quasi-compact open subsets $U_i,V_i\subseteq X$.

source.place: paragraph after Definition 08YG, line 4290 ff. ('since X is spectral an open U is retrocompact if and only if U is quasi-compact'); Definition 005G, line 2554

proof.text: Let $X^c$ be the set $X$ with its constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]. For a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X$ both $W$ and $X\setminus W$ belong to the subbase of $X^c$, so both are open in $X^c$; as they are complements of each other, both are also closed in $X^c$. So $W$ and $X\setminus W$ are open and closed in $X^c$.

source.place: paragraph after Definition 08YG (definition-spectral-space), line 4290 ff.; Definition 005G (definition-constructible, line 2554)

proof.text: In any topological space finite intersections and finite unions of open and closed subsets are open and closed (finite intersections and finite unions of open sets are open, of closed sets are closed). By step 2 each $U_i\cap(X\setminus V_i)$ is open and closed in $X^c$, and so is the finite union $E=\bigcup_{i=1}^n(U_i\cap(X\setminus V_i))$ of step 1 (for $n=0$, $E=\emptyset$ is open and closed). This proves the claim; it is the statement of Stacks that the constructible topology is the coarsest topology in which every constructible subset is open and closed, in its 'every constructible subset is open and closed' half.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against Stacks topology.tex line 4290 ff. and def-weil-constructible-subset, def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology). Proof written in three steps: (1) in a spectral space open retrocompact = quasi-compact open (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-spectral-open-retrocompact-iff-quasi-compact = QuasiSeparatedSpace.isRetrocompact_iff_isCompact, Stacks 0069 (2) and the remark after 08YG), so E is a finite union of U ∩ (X \ V) with U, V quasi-compact open (Definition 005G); (2) subbase elements W, X \ W are clopen in the constructible topology; (3) finite unions/intersections of clopens are clopen. Lemma 005H (Boolean algebra) is not needed since the finite-union form of 005G is used directly. Tags checked in tags/tags: 005G definition-constructible, 005H lemma-constructible, 0069 lemma-topology-quasi-separated-scheme, 08YG definition-spectral-space (08YF is the section).
